question: Some people think that giving offenders longer prison sentences is the best way to reduce crime. Others, however, believe that other measures are more effective. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.

Some people argue that giving scriminals longer prison terms is the best way to reduce crime. However, others believe that measures like increasing the number of security cameras are more effective. This Iessay discusses both sides of this argument and then I will give my own perspective.   The main reason for those who believe longer prison sentences is a better mway to reduce crime is that it tcan deter crime. Potential criminals who see the precedents of severe punishment on fa crime will think twice before committing acrime. Also, longer prison terms will send a clear message to those who committed crimes that the government has zero tolerance towards crimes which will prevent them from re-offending. As a result, that the crime rate could be lowered.  Furthermore, some of theC extremely dangerous criminals will be kept longer in the prisons,  which will makew local communities safer.  However, others believe that increasing the number of security cameras are more effective because it will help apolice department to itracge criminals in a costeffective and labour-effective manner. For example, the number of police officers in the  population in China is less than 1% which is much less compared with the United States. However, the crime rate in China is much lower due to the mature and well-established security camera network. AI technologies enable the police to track down criminals through facle recognition and license plate recognition functions which are both cost-effective and labour-effective.  In my opinion, that giving longer prison terms to criminals can deter crime in some ways. However, the agovernment needs to build more prisons and increase the headcounts for police officers to accommodate and manage more gprisoners,. I believe that increasing the numberi of security camerams is a more effective way to prevent crime. The government should also investigate the root cause for this issue  which is the inequality in the society. Bettereducation and vocational training should be provided for low-income families.

question: The money spent by governments on space programs would be better spent on vital public services such as schools and hospitals. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay: In contemporary society, investing a large sum of money on space programs is favored by many countries. However, some people argue that the money should be used in public services rather than space missions. As for me, I agree with the claim from these peopleconsidering two major reasons.  First of all, it is uncertain whether the outcomes of the investment on space programs will be beneficial to the national economy or the opposite may happenAdmittedly, exploring the universe and exploiting the resources in outer space can provide the nation and the society with long-term profits, but the large expenditure will also become huge burdens for governments, thereby doing huge gharm to the economy in short term. For example, Soviet once invested considerable money on the space programs in order to compete with the U.S in the universe, which involved the government in endless financial problems, contributing to the fall of this superpower. Therefore, the large fortune sgiven to space missions may turn out to be disastrous to the economy and stability of the nation.  By comparison, expending more money on public service is bound to improve the public well-being, as the social equality may be achieved gradually with more ifacilities added. For instance, in many developing countries such as India and China, the shortage of educational resources causes unfair distribution in the society. Children in big cities receive education from qualified public schools, whereas those living in poverty-stricken areas can hardly afford to attend these institutions, thus causing great difference in learning standards among the youth. Such gap can even be wider when these young people step into job markets, twhereby increasing inequality in the society. Nevertheless, if the government spent more money on building standard schools in backwards lregions, this inequality can reduced to a large degree.  In conclusion, regarding the possible negative effects caused by huge expenditure on space missions as well as the positive transformation that may be supported by the money saved, I am in firm belief that more money should be given to those public service like building more schools than the space exploration or exploitation.
